name: 2018 Prairie Avenue — three-storey brick house with a stone front and a two-storey stone bow, K01 frontage assembly

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3 brick dwelling (D), long and narrow, with a stone bay on its Prairie front'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1842 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

research_note: T-3607 (piece 1 of T-1910) refines the district draft (T-2351) in place under the same id: the main body is rebuilt from the K01 frontage assembly and its kits — K03 common brick on the flanks and rear behind a dressed brown-sandstone front, K06 sash, K07 door and stoop under a stone porch on columns, K08 bays (the stone bow on the front, the full-height step on the north flank, a canted bay on each flank and a one-storey frame bay on the north), K09 window heads, K10 bracketed cornice, K01's flat roof and three plain stacks — with the sheet's one-storey frame rear porch on K01's rear wings in timber. What is read: the 1911 Sanborn sheet 35 raster read at full size through the T-1250 fit (0.186 m a pixel; the fit's own residual 0.05 m RMS, plus about a pixel of reading), through the T-1842 census (s35-2018-front: '3 brick dwelling (D), long and narrow, with a stone bay on its Prairie front'; s35-2018-wing) — three storeys, brick with a stone front, the main body's lines (24.07 m from the rear wall to the front wall, 8.08 m across behind the front block and 8.83 m across it), the bow's place, size and '2' storeys, the porch's place, size and '1' storey, both canted flank bays, the frame bay and the frame rear porch. The draft's rectangle fit (21.25 x 5.5 m) stopped short because the trace takes the stone front for a separate part and the printed figures beside both side walls for bites out of the house. Everything above the plan — heights, openings, ornament, roof, colours — is reconstructed (liberty L-k01-2018-stone-front-3607); no picture of this house is held.

documented_range.note: The house claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws it and the T-1842 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are not read.

position.symbolic_location: 2018 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_2000 (data/street_grid/1904.json), west side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 20th to 22nd Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 35).
position.note: The rear corner of the main body on its south side (raster column 586, row 595.5), read off the 1911 sheet 35 raster at full size (T-3607) through the T-1250 fit of the sheet, which carries no independent check: its own fit residual is 0.05 m RMS on its control crossings, plus about a pixel (0.19 m) of reading on this copy. Rotation -0.379 degrees lays the plan's u axis on the sheet's own side walls (the draft's -0.593 squared it to the lot, 0.21 degrees off the walls the sheet draws). The draft's corner stood 1.15 m north of the south wall the sheet draws.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; this position is read off the sheet 35 raster through its committed fit (docs/RESEARCH/k01-2018-stone-front-3607/README.md).

footprint.note: The main body, the three-storey brick block the sheet draws: 24.07 m from the rear wall to the front wall and 8.08 m from the south wall to the north wall behind the front block, read at full size off the raster. The front block's 0.75 m step out on the north is K08's full-height projection (bays). The draft drew it 21.25 x 5.5 m, because the trace reads the stone front as a separate part and the printed figures near both side walls as bites out of the house.

stories.note: '3' printed on the 1911 sheet (s35-2018-front): three full storeys. The sheet prints no 'B'; the raised principal floor over a basement is reconstructed (principal_floor_m).

construction.note: The sheet colours the house brick with a stone front (blue across the whole front, 1.1 m deep) — the register's frontage row frontage-35-061 'Stone-front masonry'. Built as K01's brick_with_stone_front: the K03 common brick on the flanks and rear, the street front in dressed stone (stone_front).

principal_floor_m.note: A raised principal floor over a basement, inside the K01 contract's range [0.8, 1.8]: the stone porch the sheet draws at the door is a stoop's landing, and the ticket's brief asks for a high stoop. It solves to whole risers on the K07 stoop. No source reads it.

storey_heights_m.note: Floor to floor, diminishing upward, as 1634's and 2005's (the district's other three-storey flat-roofed fronts): a 12.3 m wall head under the cornice. No source reads this house's heights.

wall_thickness_front_m.note: A brick wall faced in stone, 18 inches, inside the contract's masonry range [0.23, 0.45] (as 1621's stone front). The sheet's stone band is the front's colour, not a thickness.

wall_thickness_side_m.note: Common brick, a 13-inch wall; the sheet prints no wall thickness for this lot.

service_wall_brick.note: The sheet colours the house brick; the fabric, bond, heads, string course and grime are the K03 library's common buff brick in common bond (the one panel k03_brick builds), not a reading of this house.

face_brick.note: T-3385: no picture of this house reads its brick. The flanks and rear are a Chicago common brick, buff run, as the palette's commonest side brick (data/components/prairie_1904/k03_face_brick.json); the front is stone, so it takes no face brick.

stone_front.note: The sheet's stone front, built in dressed brown sandstone with two rusticated base courses, the stone a Prairie Avenue front of its decade most often wore (1634's and 1636's). The sheet says stone, not which; the fabric, dressing and courses are reconstructed.

street_front_trim.note: The street front's window heads: the K09 stone lintel under a cornice hood on the two principal storeys and K01's flat stone lintel on the third, the Italianate stone front's set (1634's). No source reads this front.

wall_head.note: A K10 bracketed cornice along the street front under the flat roof's blocking course, the draft rules' family row for a flat stone front. No source reads it.

roof_form.note: K01's flat roof (k01.roof.flat, K05's k05.roof.flat_parapet, T-2350): a deck falling to the rear behind coped parapets and a blocking course, the draft's own roof for the house and the roof a long narrow three-storey brick house took. No source reads the roof.

roof_pitch_deg.note: The deck's fall to the rear, inside K05's flat band, as 1634's and 2005's.

eave_overhang_m.note: How far the street cornice projects under the blocking course, inside the flat roof's 0.3-1.0 m, as 1634's.

stair_landing_depth_m.note: The porch's floor: the landing at the head of the stoop runs out 2.3 m, as far as the sheet draws the stone porch (2.32 m), with a terrace either side of the flight carrying it to the porch's ends.

stoop_width_m.note: The stoop between the porch's columns: the sheet's porch is 2.98 m across, so a 1.4 m flight stands clear of both columns.

entrance_bay.note: The door at the north end of the front, where the sheet draws the one-storey stone porch ('1', 2.98 m across and 2.32 m out from the front) beside the bow; the bow fills the rest of the front, so the door can stand nowhere else on it.

front_bays.note: Two columns across the front, south to north: the bow's centre (s 3.05) and the door with the windows over it (s 6.95), under the porch. A front this narrow behind a swelled bay has room for nothing else. No source reads it.

bays.note: The K08 bays where the 1911 sheet draws them, read at full size: the stone bow on the front ('2', a curved bay 5.95 m on its chord from the south corner, standing 1.95 m out; built 5.45 m on its chord and 1.9 m out, its south end 0.3 m in from the corner, the kit's least pier), the front block's step 0.75 m out on the north flank (the sheet draws it 6.6 m long; built 6.0 m, the longest pavilion K08 stands flush with a corner, and stone-faced, as the sheet colours the front), a canted brick bay on each flank (the north one 5.0 m on its chord at u 4.28-9.29, 0.84 m out; the south one 4.08 m at u 10.04-14.12, 0.65 m out) and the one-storey frame bay the sheet draws in yellow on the north flank (2.8 m at u 12.82-15.61, 0.75 m out). The flank bays' storeys are not printed: two storeys under hipped caps, and the frame bay's one, are reconstructed; so is every window.

side_bays.note: Four windows a storey in the south flank, rear to front, clear of the canted bay (u 10.04-14.12); the sheet leaves 0.75 m to the lot line here, the light a long narrow house took from its flank. No source reads them.

north_bays.note: Two windows a storey in the north flank between the canted bay, the frame bay and the front block's step, which carry their own. The north flank looks over the open side of the shared lot. No source reads them.

rear_bays.note: Two windows a storey in the rear wall, south of the frame rear porch (the wall's own s, from its north corner). No source reads them.

rear_wings.note: The one-storey frame rear porch the sheet draws in yellow ('1') at the rear wall's north end, 2.04 m deep and 2.78 m along the wall, built on K01's rear wings in painted timber as 1613's (T-2417). Its windows and roof are reconstructed.

sash_by_storey.note: Double-hung sash, diminishing upward, inside the contract's sash ranges, as 1634's. No source reads them.

basement_lights.note: Area lights in the front wall under the raised principal floor (reconstructed, as the basement is).

roof_covering.note: Painted tin in flat seams on the deck, K04's cover for a roof this flat, with painted tin flashings, as 1634's. No source reads it.

chimneys.note: Three plain brick stacks through the deck: two against the south wall, clear of the south bay, and one against the north wall between the canted bay and the frame bay, over the spine walls of a long house's rooms (the draft drew two). No source reads this house's chimneys.

window_kit.note: Every window from the K06 kit: two-over-two double-hung sash, the kit's commonest form, not a reading of this house; the basement lights the kit's area light.

entrance_kit.note: The K07 four-panel door under a two-light transom at the head of a straight stone stoop, under a stone porch on two columns where the sheet draws the one-storey stone porch: 2.9 m across (the sheet's 2.98 m) and 2.3 m out (2.32 m). The porch's place and size are read; its columns, cornice, stone balustrade and the door are reconstructed. front_yard_m is the street grid's own distance: the front stands 9.75 m behind the Prairie Avenue street line (the draft's street_u carried into this frame) and the walk begins 1 ft further out.

boundary.note: No boundary across the front, a STATED RECONSTRUCTION: no picture of this front is held and the district draft stood none. The lot's south side is parcel prairie_2000's south line (data/street_grid/1904.json) in this frame; the parcel is one 199 ft lot for 2000, 2010 and 2018, so the north edge of this house's yard (1.2 m past its front block) is reconstructed.

yard.note: No picture of this front is held. The walk is the K14 kit's: flags from the stoop's foot, 1.2 m wide, straight out to the public walk. RECONSTRUCTED: its line, flags, width and wear.
